summary: The server crashes when attempting to load chunks that contain command blocks that consist of large numbers of characters within the previous output field
description: The Bug: The server crashes when attempting to load chunks that contain command blocks that consist of large numbers of characters within the previous output field. The full server console log and a crash report regarding this have been attached and can be found below. Stack Trace: [ crash-2022-04-27_10.42.38-server.txt] Description: Exception generating new chunk java.io.EOFException at java.base java.io.DataInputStream.readUnsignedShort(DataInputStream.java:346) at pq.a(SourceFile:54) at pq 1.a(SourceFile:34) at oz 1.a(SourceFile:136) at pu b.a(SourceFile:50) at pf 1.a(SourceFile:91) at oz 1.a(SourceFile:96) at pj.a(SourceFile:120) at cvr.a(SourceFile:65) at cvo.b(SourceFile:218) at cvo.a(SourceFile:231) at awt b.run(SourceFile:59) at awr.h(SourceFile:91) at awr.a(SourceFile:146) at awr.run(SourceFile:102) at java.base java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1136) at java.base java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:635) at java.base java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:833) Steps to Reproduce: - Launch a server running 22w16b that has command blocks enabled and join it. - Unlock all recipes within the game by executing the command provided below. recipe give s - Summon a repeating command block nearby that will constantly get the data of your player. setblock 3 minecraft:repeating_command_block{auto:1b,Command:"data get entity p"} - Leave the game, shut down the server, and reboot it. - Take note as to whether or not the server crashes when attempting to load chunks that contain command blocks that consist of large numbers of characters within the previous output field. Observed Behavior: The server crashes. Expected Behavior: The server would not crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch a server running version 22w16b with command blocks enabled.
2. Join the server.
3. Execute the command `recipe give @s` to unlock all recipes.
4. Summon a repeating command block nearby by executing the command `setblock 3 minecraft:repeating_command_block{auto:1b,Command:"data get entity @p"}`.
5. Leave the game.
6. Shut down the server.
7. Reboot the server.
8. Observe whether the server crashes when attempting to load chunks that contain command blocks with large numbers of characters in the previous output field.
Observed Behavior:
When the server attempts to load chunks that contain command blocks with extensive character strings in their command output, it results in a server crash. This issue manifests as an `EOFException` during the chunk generation process, as indicated by the stack trace in the crash report. Specifically, the exception occurs in the `DataInputStream.readUnsignedShort` method, suggesting that the server encounters an unexpected end of file while trying to read data related to the command blocks.

The problem arises when the command blocks are configured with long commands, which exceeds the expected data limits during chunk loading. As a result, the server fails to properly deserialize the chunk data, leading to a crash. This behavior is reproducible under the specified conditions, and it prevents the server from starting successfully if the affected chunks are within the loading range. 

Developers should note that this issue is specifically linked to the character length of commands within command blocks and may not occur with shorter command strings. The server should ideally handle command blocks with long outputs without crashing, allowing for smoother gameplay and chunk loading.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to load chunks containing command blocks with extensive character data in the previous output field, the server should successfully load those chunks without crashing. The command blocks should function normally, allowing players to interact with them without any interruptions or errors. This behavior should be consistent across all relevant game versions, ensuring a stable server experience when handling complex command block setups.
